scope: Evidence-derived formulation hypothesis for reproducible candidate-space formalization, hierarchical region-to-refinement design, replay benchmarking and future Agent ranking. This is not a trained predictor and not a mechanistic law.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

coordinate_systems.comparison_rule: Any source-reported recipe must be normalized by its own total before comparison with Agent search coordinates. Raw source parts must never be compared numerically to normalized-total wt% coordinates.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

stage_1.name: coarse_region_identification
stage_1.purpose: Test whether reasoning enters the evidence-supported resin-modified formulation family under a small controlled decision space.

stage_2.name: outcome_blind_fine_refinement
stage_2.purpose: Operationalize continuous/local refinement after the resin-modified family has been selected. This implementation supports reproducibility and future prospective use; it is not represented as the historical freeze algorithm.

domain_rule.acrylic_lower: lowest coarse design level justified by the evidence audit after excluding the reactive-only control
domain_rule.acrylic_upper: highest directly commensurate acrylic evidence anchor

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

stability_support: PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10 vs 11: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic showed 37% viscosity increase over 0.5-8 h at 121 C versus 76% for the higher-OH acrylic comparator

PAT_US20030022973A1: modifier-containing reactive-PUR examples reported different hot-melt stability values depending on tackifier/acrylic formulation; use only as directional evidence because other variables also differ
EP0293602A2: viscosity rise during prolonged elevated-temperature holding is explicitly treated as a reactive-hot-melt formulation failure mode

candidate_construction.rule: Stage 1 uses the Cartesian product of coarse acrylic/tackifier design levels. Stage 2 uses an outcome-blind fine grid inside the predeclared resin-modified region. Both stages scale the E2 normalized reactive core into the remaining total-formulation fraction.

fraction_basis_audit: See data/external_evidence_basis_audit.csv. Evidence percentages are only treated as directly commensurate numeric anchors when their denominator is represented as total-formulation or a curated equivalent; ambiguous addition-level percentages remain directional evidence.
claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The historical prospective claim is that the Agent recommendation preceded the validation outcome. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement algorithm are later reproducible formalizations and must not be conflated with the original historical freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.
